gaps.sentence: We ___ breakfast on the terrace every morning in summer.
gaps.explanation: have breakfast/lunch/dinner is the standard collocation for eating meals.

gaps.sentence: She was bitterly ___ when her proposal was rejected.
gaps.hint: adjective collocating with 'bitterly' after bad news
gaps.explanation: bitterly disappointed is the standard collocation; 'bitterly' combines with negative feelings.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her a compliment on her new hairstyle.
gaps.explanation: pay somebody a compliment is the fixed collocation for praising someone.

gaps.sentence: She has a ___ Scottish accent that is hard to miss.
gaps.explanation: a strong accent is the standard collocation; 'heavy accent' and 'deep accent' are not used.

gaps.sentence: She ___ great pride in her grandchildren's achievements.
gaps.explanation: take pride in something means to be pleased and satisfied with it.

gaps.sentence: I ___ hours yesterday trying to fix the printer, and it still doesn't work.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: to use time without any result
gaps.explanation: waste time means to spend time uselessly; the second clause shows there was no result.

gaps.sentence: It ___ no difference whether we leave today or tomorrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Make no difference' is the fixed phrase.
